# Exercise 1


a) 
```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)

aux <- read_xpt("AUX_I.xpt")
demo <- read_xpt("DEMO_I.xpt")

data <- inner_join(aux, demo, by = "SEQN")
print(nrow(data))
print(ncol(data))
```

b) We’ll be using the following variables. Clean up each - ensure all missing values are actually NA (rather than 999 or something), and if it’s categorical, convert it to factor with informative levels.

```{r}
data <- data[!is.na(data$INDHHIN2), ]
data <- data[!is.na(data$RIAGENDR), ]
data <- data[!is.na(data$DMDHHSZA), ]
data <- data[!is.na(data$DMDCITZN), ]
```

```{r}
hist(data$RIAGENDR)
```
```{r}
hist(data$DMDCITZN)
```
```{r}
hist(data$DMDHHSZA)
```

```{r}
hist(data$INDHHIN2)
```

c)

```{r}

model_1R <- glm(AUAREQC ~ RIAGENDR, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = data)
model_2R <- glm(AUAREQC ~ RIAGENDR + factor(DMDCITZN) + DMDHHSZA + INDHHIN2, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = data)

model_1L <- glm(AUALEQC ~ RIAGENDR, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = data)
model_2L <- glm(AUAREQC ~ RIAGENDR + factor(DMDCITZN) + DMDHHSZA + INDHHIN2, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = data)

```

```{r}

library(knitr)
library(pscl)

build_metrics <- function(model) {
  c(IRR = exp(coef(model)["RIAGENDR"]),N   = nobs(model),R2  = pR2(model)["McFadden"],AIC = model$aic)
}


df <- data.frame(
  Model_1R = build_metrics(model_1R),
  Model_2R = build_metrics(model_2R),
  Model_1L = build_metrics(model_1L),
  Model_2L = build_metrics(model_2L)
)

df_flipped <- as.data.frame(t(df))

kable(df_flipped, col.names = c("Incidence Risk Ratio", "Sample Size", "R2", "AIC"), digits = 3)

```


d)
```{r}
summary(model_2L)
library(marginaleffects)
avg_predictions(model_2L, variables = "RIAGENDR")
```
We therefore conclude that males have a bigger predicted risk ratio. It is statistically significant, [1.26, 1.36] vs [1.12, 1.21].

# Exercise 2

a)

```{r}
library(DBI) 
library(dplyr)
library(microbenchmark)

db <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "sakila_master.db")

#1)

v1 <- function() {
results <- dbGetQuery(db, "
    SELECT store.store_id, customer_list.notes
    FROM store 
    JOIN customer_list ON store.store_id = customer_list.SID 
    JOIN customer ON customer.customer_id = customer_list.ID
  ")
  
  total <- results %>% 
    group_by(store_id) %>% 
    summarise(total_customers = n(),
              average_active = mean(notes == "active", na.rm = TRUE),.groups = "drop")
  
  return(total)

}


#2)

v2 <- function() {
results <- dbGetQuery(db, "SELECT AVG( CASE WHEN customer_list.notes = 'active' THEN 1.0 ELSE 0 END) AS average_active, COUNT(customer_list.ID) AS total FROM store JOIN customer_list on store.store_id = customer_list.SID JOIN customer on customer.customer_id = customer_list.ID GROUP BY store.store_id")
print(results)
}

microbenchmark(v1 = v1(), v2 = v2())

```
Only SQL is faster. 

b)

```{r}

v1 <- function() {
results <- dbGetQuery(db, "SELECT * FROM staff_list")

total <- results[, c("name", "country")]
}

v2 <- function() {
results <- dbGetQuery(db, "SELECT staff_list.name, staff_list.country FROM staff_list")
}

microbenchmark(v1 = v1(), v2 = v2())

```
Only SQL is marginally faster.

c)


```{r}

v1 <- function() {
results <- dbGetQuery(db, "SELECT * FROM film_list")
results <- results[results$price == max(results$price),]
results <- unique(results$title)
}

v2 <- function() {
results <- dbGetQuery(db, "SELECT DISTINCT title FROM film_list WHERE film_list.price = (SELECT MAX(price) from film_list)")
  
}

microbenchmark(v1 = v1(), v2 = v2())

```
Only SQL is faster.

# Exercise 3



```{r}
data <- read.csv("au-500.csv")
```


a)

```{r}
match_indices <- grep(".com$", data$web)
print(length(match_indices) / nrow(data))

```
b)

```{r}

pattern <- "@([^@]+)$"

match_rows <- regexpr(pattern, data$email, perl = TRUE)
domains <- regmatches(data$email, match_rows)

domains <- gsub("@", "", domains)
most_frequent <- names(which.max(table(domains)))
print(most_frequent)
                       
```
c)
```{r}
match_indices <- grep("[^a-zA-Z0-9 ]", data$company_name)
print(length(match_indices) / nrow(data))
```
d)

```{r}

format_to_cell <- function(phone_col) {
  clean_digits <- gsub("\\D", "", phone_col)
  gsub("(\\d{4})(\\d{3})(\\d{3})", "\\1-\\2-\\3", clean_digits)
}

data$phone1 <- format_to_cell(data$phone1)
data$phone2 <- format_to_cell(data$phone2)

head(data[, c("phone1", "phone2")], 10)
```

e)

```{r}
library(stringr)

pattern <- "(?i)(apt|apartment|unit|#)\\s*([a-z0-9-]+)"

df <- data %>% mutate(apt_full = str_extract(address, pattern))

df <- df %>% mutate(apt_cleaned = as.integer(str_remove(apt_full, "#")))

print(df)
hist(log(df$apt_cleaned), na.rm = TRUE)
```

f)
```{r}
library(stringr)

pattern <- "(?i)(apt|apartment|unit|#)\\s*([a-z0-9-]+)"

df <- data %>% mutate(apt_full = str_extract(address, pattern))

df <- df %>% mutate(apt_cleaned = as.integer(substr(str_remove(apt_full, "#"), 1, 1)))

print(df)

hist(df$apt_cleaned, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Yes, we see 1 is the most common - so it is followed.
